newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA'S CONGRESS WANTS PRO-POOR ECONOMIC REFORMS.
newsitem.headline: INDIA'S CONGRESS WANTS PRO-POOR ECONOMIC REFORMS.

text.p: India's Congress party will recommit itself to economic reform at a crucial party meeting but stress that liberalisation must help ease poverty, party leaders said.

"We are reaffirming our commitment to reforms including financial sector reforms," former finance minister Manmohan Singh told Reuters late on Thursday in the eastern city of Calcutta, where Congress's three-day plenary session opens on Friday.
Asked about the economic resolution to be adopted at the meeting, Singh said: "We are going to move forward. We are not going to move backwards."
Singh, a free-market proponent, launched sweeping liberalisation policies in 1991 under former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, opening up trade and industry after decades of socialist controls.
Congress will adopt resolutions on political, economic and international issues at the session.
The resolutions were finalised at a meeting of party leaders late on Thursday that was chaired by party president Sitaram Kesri.
They will be moved for adoption at a meeting of the decision-making Congress Working Committee (CWC).
Singh said economic policies must aim to reduce poverty, improve education and empower the poor.
"We must move forward, accelerate the move towards removal of poverty, helping the poor people, and economic reform must assist in that process," Singh said.
"That has always been the stand of the Congress party."
Congress leaders said the party was in favour of economic reforms with a "human face".
"The economic resolution will definitely be pro-poor," said Congress general secretary Ghulam Nabi Azad.
